title: The Day Bread Stopped Being Bread: What a Second Language Really Changes
title_zh: 面包不再是面包的那一天：第二语言真正改变了什么
intro_zh: 本文约571词，共8段。文章从留学生在柏林厨房里的一个小发现出发，谈到学外语对思维方式、注意力、老年记忆、倾听习惯和实际机会的几层好处，配有6个CET-4核心词的音标与释义，文末有4道阅读理解题。

paragraphs.en: In a small kitchen in Berlin, a Chinese student named Lin picked up a packet of flour and read the word on the label: Brot. She had known the English word bread for ten years. But standing there, she suddenly understood what no teacher had told her. Brot is not bread. It is darker, heavier, sliced thick for a cold breakfast. One small word had quietly carried a whole way of eating.
paragraphs.zh: 在柏林的一间小厨房里，一位姓林的中国留学生拿起一袋面粉，读着包装上的那个词：Brot。她认识英语单词 bread 已经十年了。但站在那里的时候，她忽然明白了一件没有老师告诉过她的事。Brot 并不等于 bread。它颜色更深、分量更重、切得更厚，是配寒冷早餐吃的。一个小小的词，悄悄承载了一整套饮食方式。

paragraphs.en: This is the first gift a new language gives you: words do not line up neatly, one for one. English manages with a single verb, know, whether you mean a person or a fact. Chinese needs two. Once you have translated between them a few times, you slowly absorb a simple truth: your own language is not a transparent window on the world. It is a lens, with a shape of its own.
paragraphs.zh: 这是新语言给你的第一份礼物：词语并不是一词对一词、整整齐齐地排好的。英语只用一个动词 know，不管你说的是认识一个人还是知道一件事；汉语则需要两个。当你在两种语言之间翻译过几次之后，你会慢慢领会一个简单的道理：你自己的语言并不是一扇透明的窗户，它是一块有自己形状的镜片。

paragraphs.en: The second gift is quieter and slower to arrive. In a study at the University of Edinburgh, researchers followed more than 800 people into their seventies. Those who had learned a second language, even after the age of eighteen, scored better on tests of attention and flexible thinking — the ability to switch focus without losing the thread. The advantage was not dramatic, but it was steady.
paragraphs.zh: 第二份礼物更安静，来得也更慢。在爱丁堡大学的一项研究中，研究者追踪了八百多人一直到他们七十多岁。那些学过第二语言的人——哪怕是在十八岁之后才学的——在注意力和灵活思维的测试中得分更高；所谓灵活思维，就是能够转换注意力又不丢掉思路的能力。这种优势并不惊人，但很稳定。

paragraphs.en: Other research looks at what happens much later in life. The psychologist Ellen Bialystok studied 648 patients with a serious memory illness. The bilingual patients, who used two languages every day, showed the first symptoms about four years later than patients who spoke only one. Bialystok is careful with her words: a second language does not prevent the illness. It seems to build a reserve that hides the damage for longer.
paragraphs.zh: 另一些研究关注的是人生更晚阶段的状况。心理学家埃伦·比亚韦斯托克研究了648位患有严重记忆疾病的病人。那些每天使用两种语言的双语病人，初次出现症状的时间比只说一种语言的病人晚大约四年。比亚韦斯托克措辞很谨慎：第二语言并不能预防这种疾病，它似乎只是积累起一种储备，让损伤被隐藏得更久一些。

paragraphs.en: Why should talking help the brain? Because using two languages is a daily exercise in stopping yourself. Every time a bilingual person opens their mouth, both languages wake up at once, and the mind must hold one down while the other speaks. That happens hundreds of times a day, in ordinary conversation, with no special training. It is less like lifting weights and more like a traffic officer guiding two busy lanes into one.
paragraphs.zh: 为什么说话会对大脑有帮助？因为使用两种语言本身就是一种天天进行的自我克制练习。双语者每次开口，两套语言会同时被唤醒，大脑必须压住其中一套，让另一套说话。这在普通日常对话中每天要发生几百次，而且不需要任何专门训练。它不太像在健身房举重，更像是交警把两条繁忙的车道并成一条。

paragraphs.en: There is a social benefit too, and it is easy to overlook. Learning a language makes people better listeners. When you are unsure of a word, you ask again; you watch faces and hands; you accept being slow. A Chinese engineer on a joint project said the sentence he used most was: 'Sorry, could you say that again, more slowly?' He expected to lose face. Instead his foreign colleagues trusted him more, because he never pretended to understand.
paragraphs.zh: 还有一层社交上的好处，很容易被忽略。学一门外语会让人更会倾听。当你拿不准某个词时，你会再问一遍；你会去看对方的表情和手势；你能接受自己慢一点。一位参加联合项目的中国工程师说，他用得最多的一句话是："抱歉，你能再说一遍吗，慢一点？"他本以为会丢面子，结果外国同事反而更信任他，因为他从不假装听懂了。

paragraphs.en: Then there are the practical rewards. A second language widens the shelf of books, films and news you can reach without a translator. In Europe, more than half of adults say they can hold a conversation in a language other than their mother tongue, and many jobs quietly expect it. The skill rarely appears on a list of requirements; it simply makes doors open a little more easily.
paragraphs.zh: 接着是实际的好处。第二语言会拓宽你的书架：书、电影、新闻，你不必借助翻译就能直接接触。在欧洲，超过一半的成年人说自己能用母语之外的语言交谈，而许多工作岗位会悄悄地对这一点有所期待。这项能力很少出现在招聘要求的清单上，它只是让门打开得稍微容易一些。

paragraphs.en: None of this arrives quickly. The gains are gradual, and the first months can feel like walking uphill in sand. But fifteen honest minutes a day, kept up for a year, will change how you hear the world. The reward is not perfect grammar. It is a second pair of eyes, and a small permanent doubt about the idea that your first language is the only one that describes things correctly.
paragraphs.zh: 这一切都不会来得很快。收获是渐进的，头几个月感觉像在沙子里上坡。但每天实实在在的十五分钟，坚持一年，就会改变你听世界的方式。回报并不是完美的语法，而是第二双眼睛，以及一种小小的、长久的怀疑：怀疑"你的母语是唯一能正确描述事物的语言"这个想法。

questions.q: What is the passage mainly about?
options: How to memorize foreign words in a short time
The wider benefits that learning a second language brings
The differences between European and Chinese eating habits
Why adults usually fail to learn a new language
questions.explain: 主旨题。全文从柏林厨房的小故事入手，依次讲外语带来的认知、防老、社交、实际机会等层面的好处，因此B正确。A、D文中未讨论，C只是开头的引子。

questions.q: According to the study at the University of Edinburgh, people who learned a second language in adulthood
options: did better on tests of attention and flexible thinking
were more likely to travel and live abroad
could pick up new words faster than children
questions.explain: 细节题。第三段明确说明，十八岁以后学第二语言的人在注意力和灵活思维测试中得分更高，并且这种优势稳定，故选B。其余三项在文中均无依据。

questions.q: What can be inferred from Bialystok's findings?
options: Bilingual people never develop memory illness.
A second language may delay the visible signs of a brain illness rather than prevent it.
Patients with memory problems should stop learning languages.
Only languages learned in childhood protect the brain.
questions.explain: 推断题。第四段强调她措辞谨慎：第二语言并不预防疾病，而是积累一种储备，使损伤被隐藏得更久，即推迟症状出现，故选B。A、C、D都与原文相反或无依据。

questions.q: The word 'reserve' in paragraph 4 is closest in meaning to
options: a supply kept for later use
a booking for a seat or room
questions.explain: 词义题。此处 reserve 指大脑中逐渐积累起来的一种"储备"，让损伤更晚显现，与A"留待日后使用的储备"最接近。B、C、D分别是该词的其他常见义项，不符合语境。
